comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts and validates damper response on an isolated robot axis; record installs and snaps shut a personal padlock on an occupied group-lockout hasp while preserving energy isolation.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate uses a removable hex key, counterhold, controlled fastener torque, collar rotation, tool re-engagement, and iterative dynamic diagnosis. Record grasps and reorients an open padlock, aligns its shackle through two moving hasp jaws, latches it, and avoids disturbing an existing lock.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires relocking followed by two repeatable, non-bottoming cycles and a witness-torque drift check. Record requires the closed purple lock to remain effective after release under 0.3 N·m hasp-pry and 1.5 N·m handle tests, with strict coworker-lock, jaw-opening, and handle-motion hazards.
comparison.reason: Both involve safety-sensitive bimanual alignment and latching/retention, but one tests adjustable damping plus iterative physical response control; the other tests through-hole shackle insertion and lockout retention. All eight spec versions were read and preserve that distinction. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, locking-torque, and drift-tolerance thresholds; the record does not penalize dropping the purple lock itself, but neither gap suggests duplication.
